subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should ordinary plugin runtime code be allowed to call plugin-registered Gateway methods, and what caller identity, allowlist, and authorization model should that API use?
rationale: The request changes both the public Plugin SDK and the Gateway method authorization boundary, so automation cannot safely choose between raw dispatch, curated accessors, or typed service/capability contracts.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
options.body: Expose approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep dispatch limited to HTTP routes
options.body: Decline ordinary plugin-to-plugin Gateway calls and require plugins to use existing HTTP route, runtime helper, or capability seams.

options.title: Expose raw Gateway dispatch
options.body: Add a generic method-string caller and accept the larger security and compatibility surface as a maintainer-owned product decision.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
recommendation.body: Expose approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest history on both the existing Gateway method dispatch contract and the original plugin architecture surface.
